headline: PaperCut two-flaw chain exploited via CVE-2026-81578 & CVE-2026-82078
summary: Two critical vulnerabilities in PaperCut NG/MF, rated 9.8 and 9.1, allow unauthenticated code execution. These flaws have been actively exploited by foreign agents, impacting hundreds of organizations globally.
details: CISA added CVE-2026-81578 (CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (CVSS 9.1) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 31, 2026, with a September 14 remediation deadline. These flaws in PaperCut NG/MF allow unauthenticated requests to reach management functionality and unsafe dynamic class loading.

The first flaw (CVE-2026-81578) is an improper access control vulnerability, allowing unauthenticated access to the web management interface. The second (CVE-2026-82078) is an unsafe reflection vulnerability in database connection utilities, enabling an attacker to load a controlled class.
Chaining these two flaws results in code execution within the paper management service. On Windows, this service often runs as SYSTEM, providing a direct route into the domain.

Public reports describe a foreign agent-operated intrusion campaign that quickly affected hundreds of internet-exposed instances across dozens of countries, particularly in education. The campaign focused on credential extraction, lateral movement, and directory database replication.

PaperCut has released emergency patches for affected branches; users should confirm the latest recommended patch level rather than the first one published. Administrators must also review database driver configurations for unauthorized values and export application/OS logs to an external system.

Given the high privileges of the PaperCut service, compromised credentials are a significant risk. Organizations should prioritize assessing affected accounts, administrative control, and potential credential reuse, and consider account rotation.

headline: Google's new Guided Vision helps read fine print and describe surroundings with AI
summary: Guided Vision uses Gemini Live on Android devices to provide real-time audio descriptions of objects and text, designed for people with low vision.
details: Google has launched Guided Vision, a new AI feature in Gemini Live that provides real-time audio descriptions of what your phone's camera sees. Available today on compatible Android devices, it assists users with low vision in daily tasks.

Users can point their phone's camera at objects or text to get audio descriptions, helping with tasks like reading small print, identifying items, or understanding surroundings. It leverages Google's Gemini AI for detailed insights.

Similar to Apple's VoiceOver Live Recognition, Guided Vision is also integrated into Google TalkBack and can be set up via an accessibility shortcut on Android 9+ devices. It was announced as part of recent Pixel updates.

The feature supports follow-up questions, allowing users to ask for specific details like an expiration date. Google advises against using it for critical tasks such as navigation or obstacle detection, as it's not a replacement for mobility aids.
